**ENG Drawing Viewer 2.3.0 for Macs with Apple silicon, Windows x64 and Linux x86-64.** A free, offline workspace for engineering drawings: view folders of PDF drawings and images sharply at any zoom, mark them up with numbered review comments, turn them into PowerPoint slides, edit images, vectors and PDFs, and use 32 PDF tools, all on your own computer.

## Install and first launch

1. Open the DMG and drag **ENG Drawing Viewer** onto **Applications**.
2. Open the app. It is ad-hoc signed only: it has no Apple Developer ID signature and is **not notarized by Apple**, so macOS says it could not verify the app. Click **Done**.
3. Open **System Settings › Privacy & Security**, scroll down, click **Open Anyway** next to the message about ENG Drawing Viewer, and confirm with your password or Touch ID.

You do this once. You do not need to turn off Gatekeeper or any other system security setting.

### Windows

1. Download `ENG-Drawing-Viewer-Windows-x64.zip`, right-click it › **Extract All**, open the folder and run `ENG Drawing Viewer.exe`. No installation or administrator rights are needed.
2. The app is not code-signed, so SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC": click **More info › Run anyway**.

### Linux

```bash
chmod +x ENG-Drawing-Viewer-Linux-x86_64.AppImage
./ENG-Drawing-Viewer-Linux-x86_64.AppImage
```

Without FUSE (`fusermount3`), run it with `--appimage-extract-and-run`. **Help › Add to Applications Menu** creates a menu entry. The file is not signed; check its SHA-256.

**Check your download:**

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing   # macOS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing       # Linux
```

On Windows: `Get-FileHash ENG-Drawing-Viewer-Windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256` in PowerShell.

## What's in it

- **View:** folders and nested subfolders of PDFs and images, thumbnails, sheet sizes, natural sorting, sharp tiled rendering from 1.5 % to 4800 %.
- **MARK:** pen, highlighter, arrow, circle, text, eraser and numbered callouts with linked, spell-checked comments; undo and redo; copy the marked page or save it as a PDF with vector markup. The original PDF is never changed.
- **PowerPoint:** queue pages and export editable `.pptx` slides without PowerPoint; marked pages put the drawing on the right and the numbered comments on the left.
- **New in 2.3.0: Image Editor, Vector Editor and Edit PDF:** layered image editing with background removal and Quick Selection, real SVG/DXF vector editing with raster tracing, and PDF editing with genuine redaction.
- **PDF Tools:** 32 offline tools to organize, convert, optimize, edit, secure and compare drawings. *Office to PDF* needs LibreOffice installed.
- **Private:** no account, no telemetry, no network connections.

## Built and checked

- Built from the published source archive with Python 3.13 and hash-checked dependencies. Every ENG Drawing Viewer Python module in the app was compared with that archive and is identical.
- 308 automated tests passed on Apple silicon; the 16 skipped tests are for Windows, Linux or Windows OCR data.
- The packaged app was started on an Apple M3 Max with macOS 27.0.1: it rendered a drawing, ran the PDF tools and the editor checks, left the original file unchanged, and it and its worker processes held 0 network sockets.
- macOS 14.4 is the highest minimum declared by any bundled binary. This build has been run on macOS 27.0.1 only; the 2.2 builds ran on macOS 14.8, 15.7 and 26.6.
- OpenCV is a minimal build from source (core, imgproc, photo), so the app contains no FFmpeg and no OpenSSL.
- **Windows and Linux:** built from the published Windows/Linux source archive with the same application code (identical to the Apple silicon edition). Windows: 322 automated tests passed (13 skipped for other platforms); Linux: 323 passed (12 skipped). Both packaged apps started, rendered a drawing, ran the PDF tools and the editor checks, left the original unchanged and held 0 network sockets (Windows on Windows Server 2025 with outbound traffic blocked; Linux on Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04, Debian 12, Fedora 42 and Rocky Linux 9, inside a network namespace without a network). Both contain a minimal OpenCV built from source and no FFmpeg or OpenSSL 1.1.1k.
- No AI model is included. Optional model packs are installed by you from local files.
- Every bundled component and its licence is listed in the app under **Help › About › Third-Party Notices**.

## Known issues

- The **Read Me** on the disk image still opens with a line left over from testing that calls this a "private development candidate". It is the public 2.3.0 release; the line will go in the next build.
- **Windows and Linux have been checked by automated tests and scripted desktop sessions (a CI Windows desktop, Xvfb, headless Wayland), not yet by a person on an everyday Windows 10/11 PC or a GNOME/KDE desktop.** Windows has run on Windows Server 2025 only in this round. Please report problems in Issues.
- The Linux edition contains NumPy's libquadmath (LGPL-2.1); the nearest upstream GCC source is attached, see `THIRD_PARTY_SOURCES.txt`.
- The workspaces have been exercised by automated tests and the packaged smoke test, not yet by a person clicking through the packaged app.

Changes in detail: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/ca-works/eng-drawing-viewer/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
